newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE smashes drug ring making mandrax pills.
newsitem.headline: UAE smashes drug ring making mandrax pills.

text.p: United Arab Emirates police have smashed a drug ring of Indian and Pakistani nationals and seized six million mandrax tablets which they had produced for sale in the Gulf Arab state and abroad, newspapers reported.

On Wednesday they quoted Dubai's police chief Major General Dhahi Khalfan Tamim as saying 10 Pakistanis and Indians were arrested when police raided four factories and several storage facilities in Dubai and two other UAE emirates -- Umm al-Quwain and Sharjah. Two gang members were still at large.
He said five million pills of the banned sedative were found in Umm al-Quwain and one million pills in Dubai.
"The men involved in the manufacture of mandrax pills were tracked down before they could begin exporting the drug," he said.
The newspapers said the confiscated drugs had a street value of 90 million dirhams ($24.5 million).
The UAE imposes the death penalty on convicted drug traffickers and dealers.
In some countries mandrax is usually sold as pills which are crushed to powder and combined with marijuana in a cocktail which produces calmness and feelings of well-being when smoked.
The drug, a highly addictive sedative, is mainly produced illegally in India.
